*   2 June: [CTC-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTC_(TV_station) "CTC (TV station)")[Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra "Canberra") officially commences transmissions.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sc10snsw-29)
*   1 July: [Frank Packer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Packer "Frank Packer") (owner of TCN-9 Sydney) buys GTV-9 Melbourne, forming the [National Television Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network"), the first in the country.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   13 July: [DDQ-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTQ "RTQ")[Toowoomba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toowoomba "Toowoomba") begins transmission.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-winqld-31)
*   1 November: [TNQ-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNQ "TNQ") launches in [Townsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Townsville "Townsville").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sevenqld-32)
*   18 December: [ABC-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_(TV_station) "ABC (TV station)") Canberra launches.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-abc50s60s-21)

1963
*   7 September: [RTQ-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTQ-7 "RTQ-7")[Rockhampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockhampton "Rockhampton") begins broadcasting.

1964
*   19 June: [RVN-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMV_(TV_station) "AMV (TV station)")[Wagga Wagga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagga_Wagga "Wagga Wagga") launches.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime60s-26)
*   1 August: [ATV-0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATV_(Australia) "ATV (Australia)"), [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne")'s third commercial station, launches.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   7 September: [AMV-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMV_(TV_station) "AMV (TV station)")[Albury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albury,_New_South_Wales "Albury, New South Wales") commences broadcasting.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime60s-26)

1965
*   23 January: [NRN-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRN-11 "NRN-11")[Coffs Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffs_Harbour "Coffs Harbour") begins broadcasting.
*   5 April: [TEN-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEN_(TV_station) "TEN (TV station)")[Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney") begins transmission.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tensyd-33)
*   10 April: [WBQ-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STQ "STQ")[Wide Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Division_of_Wide_Bay "Division of Wide Bay")/[Maryborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryborough,_Queensland "Maryborough, Queensland")[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sevenqld-32) and [NEN-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEN_(TV_station) "NEN (TV station)")[Tamworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamworth,_New_South_Wales "Tamworth, New South Wales") begin transmission.
*   12 May: [NRN-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRN "NRN")[Coffs Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffs_Harbour "Coffs Harbour") begins broadcasting.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sc10nnsw-34)
*   12 June: [STW-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STW "STW")[Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth") opens.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-stw-35)
*   1 July: [TVQ-0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVQ "TVQ")[Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane") launches.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tenbris-36)
*   26 July: [SAS-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAS_(TV_station) "SAS (TV station)")[Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") launches.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tenbris-36)
*   27 September: [NEN-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEN_(TV_station) "NEN (TV station)")[Tamworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamworth,_New_South_Wales "Tamworth, New South Wales") begins transmission.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime60s-26)
*   27 November: [STV-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VTV_(TV_station) "VTV (TV station)")[Mildura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildura "Mildura") launches.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-winvic-24)
*   1 December: Australia's first regional television network is formed when [CWN-6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBN_(Australian_TV_station) "CBN (Australian TV station)")[Dubbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbo "Dubbo") opens as a direct relay of CBN-8 Orange.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime60s-26)
*   15 December: [MTN-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTN_(TV_station) "MTN (TV station)")[Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griffith,_New_South_Wales "Griffith, New South Wales") commences transmission.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)

1966
*   25 March: [SES-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SES/RTS "SES/RTS")[Mount Gambier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Gambier,_South_Australia "Mount Gambier, South Australia") officially launches.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   18 July: _[Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_School\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)")_ begins on ABC
*   27 May: [ECN-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEN_(TV_station) "NEN (TV station)")[Taree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taree,_New_South_Wales "Taree, New South Wales") launches.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime60s-26)
*   7 September: [FNQ-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNQ "TNQ") begins transmission in and around [Cairns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairns "Cairns").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sc10qld-37)

1967
*   10 March: [BTW-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_West_Network "Golden West Network")[Bunbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunbury,_Western_Australia "Bunbury, Western Australia") becomes the first regional television station in [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-gwn-38)
*   10 April: [ABC TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)") current affairs program _[This Day Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Day\_Tonight "This Day Tonight")_ premieres.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   15 June: Test [colour television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_television#Color_television "History of television") transmissions are made for the first time in Australia by ATV-0.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)

1968
*   [TVW-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVW "TVW") conducts its first [Telethon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telethon "Telethon").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   1 March: [GTS-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTS-4 "GTS-4")[Port Pirie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Pirie,_South_Australia "Port Pirie, South Australia") launches.
*   9 August: [MVQ-6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STQ "STQ") launches in [Mackay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackay,_Queensland "Mackay, Queensland").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sevenqld-32)
*   16 August: [BKN-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTS/BKN "GTS/BKN")[Broken Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Hill,_New_South_Wales "Broken Hill, New South Wales") opens.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-gwn-38)

1969
*   20 July: The [Apollo 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") Moon landing is televised live by [television stations in Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_broadcasting_in_Australia "Television broadcasting in Australia").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-first24-12)

*   Undated: First fully colour capable production facility opened in Sydney (Video Tape Corp, in East Roseville).

## 1970s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1970s")]

1971
*   4 January: Long running US children's educational series _[Sesame Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesame\_Street "Sesame Street")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)").
*   18 June: [VEW-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_West_Network "Golden West Network")[Kalgoorlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalgoorlie "Kalgoorlie") begins broadcasting.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-39)
*   13 August: [ABD-6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABD_(TV_station) "ABD (TV station)") launches as [Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin,_Northern_Territory "Darwin, Northern Territory")'s first television station.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His60-30)
*   11 September: [ITQ-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QQQ "QQQ")[Mount Isa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Isa "Mount Isa") begins broadcasting.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sccentral-40)
*   9 October: _[Hey Hey It's Saturday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey\_Hey\_It's\_Saturday "Hey Hey It's Saturday")_ starts off as a Saturday morning cartoon program for children on [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network").
*   22 November: _[A Current Affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Current\_Affair\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "A Current Affair (Australian TV series)")_, hosted by [Mike Willesee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Willesee "Mike Willesee"), makes its first appearance on the [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His70-41)
*   11 November: [NTD-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTD_(Australian_TV_station) "NTD (Australian TV station)") is officially launched by [Administrator of the Northern Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_the_Northern_Territory "Administrator of the Northern Territory"), [Fred Chaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Chaney "Fred Chaney").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-42)

1972
*   13 March: Soap opera _[Number 96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number\_96\_(TV\_series) "Number 96 (TV series)")_ debuts, heralding the night 'Australian television lost its virginity'
*   20 March: Brisbane channel [BTQ-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTQ "BTQ") claims Australia's first one-hour news bulletin, The Big News[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His70-41)

1973
*   In 1973, the only Australian designed and made precision colour television monitor,was produced for local use and international export. The broadcast quality monitor (LDN5006)was developed by Willem Sparrius, Project Engineer at Philips subsidiary company Electronics Engineering Communications and produced at their South Oakleigh plant.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-DoubleDutch-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-OakleighWorldHeadquarters-44)

1974
*   29 August: [GSW-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_West_Network "Golden West Network")[Albany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_Western_Australia "Albany, Western Australia") begins broadcasting as a relay of VEW-8 Kalgoorlie.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   October: Colour test transmissions begin on Australian television.
*   8 November: _[Countdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countdown\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Countdown (Australian TV series)")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)").

1975
*   1 March: At midnight, [colour television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colour_television "Colour television") is introduced across the country. The main networks celebrate with their own unique slogan – _Come to Colour_ (ABC TV), _Seven Colors Your World_ (Seven Network), _Living Color_ (Nine Network) and _0 – First in Color_ (0-10 Network).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-birth-14)

1976
*   26 November: [RTS-5A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SES/RTS "SES/RTS") Loxton launches in the [Riverland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverland "Riverland") district.

1977
*   21 January: [GTW-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_West_Network "Golden West Network")[Geraldton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldton "Geraldton") begins broadcasting, completing the roll-out of regional commercial television across Australia.
*   24 September: The _[Victorian Football League Grand Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian\_Football\_League#Premiership\_season "Australian Football League")_ is broadcast live to viewers in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") for the first time.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His70-41)

1979
*   11 February: Current affairs program _[60 Minutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60\_Minutes\_(Australian\_TV\_program) "60 Minutes (Australian TV program)")_ debuts on the [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network").
*   7 April: The [Special Broadcasting Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service") begins test transmissions on [ABV-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABV_(TV_station) "ABV (TV station)")[Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") and [ABN-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABN_(TV_station) "ABN (TV station)")[Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), with foreign-language programming shown on Sunday mornings.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His70-41)

## 1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1980s")]

1980
*   20 January: [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne,_Australia "Melbourne, Australia")'s [ATV-0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATV-0 "ATV-0") converts to [ATV-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATV-10 "ATV-10"); after nearby La Trobe Valley regional station GLV-10 converts to [GLV-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLV/BCV "GLV/BCV") to facilitate this change, which concurrently frees up the frequency for [Channel 0/28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") later that same year.
*   14 July: Game show _[Sale of the Century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sale\_of\_the\_Century\_(Australian\_game\_show) "Sale of the Century (Australian game show)")_ debuts on the [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network").
*   24 October: [Channel 0/28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") is launched by [Bruce Gyngell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Gyngell "Bruce Gyngell") in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney") and [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-birth-14)

1982
*   28 June: The [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network") Australia premieres _[Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today\_(1982\_TV\_program) "Today (1982 TV program)")_.

1983
*   1 July: The Australian Broadcasting Commission becomes the [Australian Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   16 October: Channel 0/28 expands into [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra "Canberra"), [Cooma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooma,_New_South_Wales "Cooma, New South Wales") and [Goulburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goulburn,_New_South_Wales "Goulburn, New South Wales"), and changes its name to [Network 0-28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)

1984
*   4 February: _[Hey Hey It's Saturday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey\_Hey\_It's\_Saturday "Hey Hey It's Saturday")_ moves from its morning timeslot to the 9.30 pm timeslot.
*   July: The [1984 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics "1984 Summer Olympics") are broadcast on [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten "Network Ten").
*   26 July: US-French-Canadian animated series _[Inspector Gadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inspector\_Gadget\_(1983\_TV\_series) "Inspector Gadget (1983 TV series)")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation").

1985
*   18 February: Network 0-28 once again changes its name to [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)"), and begins daytime transmissions.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)
*   4 March: _ABC National_, a one-hour national news and current affairs program shown from 6.30 pm, replaces [ABC TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)")'s half-hour 7.00pm state news bulletins.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   18 March: Soap opera _[Neighbours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbours "Neighbours")_ begins on the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network").
*   30 June: [SBS Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Television "SBS Television") expands into [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"), [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide"), [Newcastle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle,_New_South_Wales "Newcastle, New South Wales"), [Wollongong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wollongong "Wollongong"), and the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)
*   24 October: The [ABC Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation#Management "Australian Broadcasting Corporation") elects to abandon _ABC National_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)

1986
*   5 January: SBS Television phases out its second [VHF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Very_high_frequency "Very high frequency") 0 channel.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)
*   16 March: SBS launches in [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth") and [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart "Hobart").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)
*   19 August: [Treasurer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasurer_of_Australia "Treasurer of Australia")[Paul Keating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Keating "Paul Keating"), in his budget speech, announces the amalgamation of the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation") and [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)

1987
*   26 March: [Bob Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hawke "Bob Hawke") calls off the proposed amalgamation of the ABC and SBS.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   17 April: _[Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage\_(TV\_program) "Rage (TV program)")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)").
*   27 December: [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") stations SAS-10 and ADS-7 swap frequencies to become [SAS-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAS_(TV_station) "SAS (TV station)") and [ADS-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADS_(TV_station) "ADS (TV station)").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)

1988
*   1 January: [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network") first use of SNG (Satellite News Gathering) in Australia. Transmission from Kingoonya SA for Australia Live 88 which showcased Australia remotely in a four hour broadcast.
*   2 January: [Imparja Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imparja_Television "Imparja Television") launches in remote eastern and central Australia from studios in [Alice Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Springs "Alice Springs").
*   17 January: _[Home and Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home\_and\_Away "Home and Away")_ premieres on the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network") as a two-hour pilot and begins as a regular weeknight soap opera the following evening.
*   20 May: [NEW-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEW_(TV_station) "NEW (TV station)") launches in Perth.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)
*   10 September: [TVQ-0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVQ "TVQ") Brisbane becomes TVQ-10.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-His80-46)

1989
*   31 March: [Aggregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_television_in_Australia#Aggregation "Regional television in Australia") begins in southern [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales "New South Wales").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)

## 1990s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 1990s")]

1990
*   [Imparja Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imparja_Television "Imparja Television") begins producing 15-minute local news bulletins inserted into its _[National Nine News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine\_News "Nine News")_ simulcast, entitled _Imparja Local News_.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-imparja-48)
*   27 January: Long running children's wrapper program _[Saturday Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Disney "Saturday Disney")_ which airs television shows from [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") begins on [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network").
*   3 September: Children's TV series _[Johnson and Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson\_and\_Friends "Johnson and Friends")_ begins on ABC.
*   21 December: [James Valentine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Valentine_(journalist) "James Valentine (journalist)") leaves _[The Afternoon Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Afternoon\_Show\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "The Afternoon Show (Australian TV series)")_ after his final day of presenting the weekday afternoon magazine program.
*   24 December: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") purchases [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_10 "Network 10") affiliate-to-be [Star Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTQ "RTQ") and switches its affiliation to the [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network") for [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland "Queensland").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)
*   31 December: Regional [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland "Queensland") is aggregated.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)

1991
*   10 February: US animated comedy series _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_ begins on [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten "Network Ten").
*   14 June: [SBS TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") is permitted by the government to broadcast five minutes of [advertising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising "Advertising") per hour, as a form of additional funding.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sbsfive-49)
*   31 December: Northern [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales "New South Wales") is aggregated.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)

1992
*   1 January: Aggregation begins to take place in [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia) "Victoria (Australia)").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)
*   3 February: Midday news program _[The World at Noon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC\_News\_(Australia)#The\_Midday\_Report "ABC News (Australia)")_ is launched on [ABC TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   3 February: Former Europe correspondent for the ABC [Ian Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Henderson_(news_presenter) "Ian Henderson (news presenter)") takes over as newsreader for the 7.00 pm weeknights [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(Australia) "ABC News (Australia)") in Victoria.
*   8 May: An educational television series for children called _[Lift Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift\_Off\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Lift Off (Australian TV series)")_ begins being broadcast on ABC every Friday afternoon at 2:00pm. The show will later air on weekdays at 4:30pm on 29 June and on Saturday evenings at 6:00pm on 19 September.
*   20 July: Children's TV series _[Bananas in Pyjamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bananas\_in\_Pyjamas "Bananas in Pyjamas")_ begins on ABC.
*   27 November: [Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Australia "Parliament of Australia") passes a bill permitting the ABC to provide [subscription television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subscription_television "Subscription television") services.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)

1993
*   26 January: Early morning news program _[First Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC\_News\_(Australia) "ABC News (Australia)")_ begins on the ABC.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   17 February: The [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation")'s [Australia Television International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Television_International "Australia Television International") is launched by [Prime Minister of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia "Prime Minister of Australia")'s [Paul John Keating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_John_Keating "Paul John Keating").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   September: The Victorian arm of the [Southern Cross Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_(Southern_Cross_Austereo) "10 (Southern Cross Austereo)") changes its name to _SCN_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sc10vic-23)

1994
*   [Southern Cross Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Broadcasting "Southern Cross Broadcasting") purchases [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra "Canberra")-based station [Capital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTC_(TV_station) "CTC (TV station)").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sc10snsw-29)
*   20 May: [Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin,_Northern_Territory "Darwin, Northern Territory") is the last capital city to begin receiving SBS.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)
*   30 April: [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania") is aggregated, as a two-station market.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvau-aggregation-47)
*   31 July: Community station [Briz 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31_Brisbane "31 Brisbane") commences transmission.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-communitybris-50)
*   October: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") expands into [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia) "Victoria (Australia)") and [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania"), purchasing [ENT Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ENT_Limited "ENT Limited"), owners of TasTV and Vic Television.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-winvic-24)
*   6 October: Community station [C31 Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C31_Melbourne "C31 Melbourne") launches.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-communitymelb-51)

1995
*   26 January: [Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy_(Australian_television) "Galaxy (Australian television)") launches Australia's first subscription television service on MMDS.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-galaxylaunch-52)
*   19 September: Australia's first cable TV provider, [Optus Vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optus_Vision "Optus Vision"), begins broadcasting.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-optuslaunch-53)

*   22 October: Foxtel was founded and introduced into Australia.
*   4 December: State editions of _[The 7.30 Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_7.30\_Report "The 7.30 Report")_ are merged into a single national program, presented from [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABN_(TV_station) "ABN (TV station)") by [Kerry O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_O'Brien_(journalist) "Kerry O'Brien (journalist)").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)

1996
*   [Prime Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime7 "Prime7") expands into [Mildura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildura "Mildura") as PTV-31, after being granted the area's second commercial licence.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime90s-54)
*   December: Prime Television purchases the [Golden West Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GWN7 "GWN7") for $71 million.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime90s-54)

1997
*   8 July: Ownership of Australia Television International moves from the [Australian Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation") to the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   December: [Prime Television Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Media_Group "Prime Media Group") purchases [Canal 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_9_(Argentina) "Canal 9 (Argentina)") in [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime90s-54)

1998
*   16 February: UK children's television series _[Teletubbies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teletubbies "Teletubbies")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation").
*   27 March: [TND-34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TND_(TV_station) "TND (TV station)")[Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin,_Northern_Territory "Darwin, Northern Territory"), a Seven Network affiliate, is officially inaugurated by [Chief Minister of the Northern Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_the_Northern_Territory "Chief Minister of the Northern Territory"), [Shane Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Stone "Shane Stone").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tnddarwin-55)
*   10 May: Drama _[SeaChange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SeaChange "SeaChange")_ begins on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation").
*   1 July: The [WIN Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Corporation "WIN Corporation") acquires [MTN-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTN_(TV_station) "MTN (TV station)")[Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griffith,_New_South_Wales "Griffith, New South Wales") and supplementary licence AMN-31.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-winprofile-56)
*   31 July: [The Wiggles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wiggles "The Wiggles")' television show is launched on [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-57)
*   30 August: [Prime Television New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Television_New_Zealand "Prime Television New Zealand") is launched, owned by Prime Television's parent company Prime Television Limited.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime90s-54)
*   28 September: _[Pokémon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon "Pokémon")_ begins on [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten "Network Ten").
*   20 December: The [Disney Channel Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel_(Australia_and_New_Zealand) "Disney Channel (Australia and New Zealand)") premieres a TV special: The Wiggles Live at Disneyland to launch [The Wiggles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wiggles "The Wiggles")' debut.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-58)

1999
*   26 March: [WOW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WOW_(TV_station) "WOW (TV station)"), regional [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia")'s second commercial television network owned by [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television"), launches.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-wow-59)
*   18 June: Perth community station [Access 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_31 "Access 31") officially commences transmission.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-access-60)
*   15 August: [WIN South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SES/RTS "SES/RTS") is established following the buyout SES-8 Mount Gambier and RTS-5A Loxton by [WIN Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Corporation "WIN Corporation").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-winprofile-56)
*   31 December: [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)") is the Australian broadcaster of the global television event _[2000 Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000\_Today "2000 Today")_.

## 2000s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2000s")]

2000[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG/250px-2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG)

The [Sydney 2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") opening ceremony becomes one of the highest-rating programs in Australian television history.

*   15 September: The [2000 Summer Olympics Opening Ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Opening_Ceremony "2000 Summer Olympics Opening Ceremony") is broadcast by the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network") – one of the highest-rating programs ever shown on [Australian television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_television "Australian television").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime00s-61)

2001
*   1 January: [Digital terrestrial television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_terrestrial_television_in_Australia "Digital terrestrial television in Australia") is introduced to audiences in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"), [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") and [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-730report-62)
*   8 June: [Prime Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Television "Prime Television") axes local news services in [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra "Canberra"), [Wollongong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wollongong "Wollongong") and [Newcastle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle,_New_South_Wales "Newcastle, New South Wales").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime00s-61)
*   4 September: [Southern Cross Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Broadcasting "Southern Cross Broadcasting") acquires Telecasters Australia, gaining control of [Ten Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNQ "TNQ"), [Ten Northern NSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRN "NRN"), [Seven Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TND_(TV_station) "TND (TV station)") and [Seven Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QQQ "QQQ").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-63)
*   1 August: [ABC Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australia) "ABC Television (Australia)") launches its first digital-only multichannel, [ABC Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   1 November: [Fly TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly_TV "Fly TV") launches, sharing bandwidth with ABC Kids.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   22 November: [Ten Capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTC_(TV_station) "CTC (TV station)")'s local news bulletin, _[Ten Capital News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten\_Capital\_News "Ten Capital News")_, is axed.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tencapitalnews-64)

2002
*   18 February: [Prime Television New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Television_New_Zealand "Prime Television New Zealand") and [Publishing and Broadcasting Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishing_and_Broadcasting_Limited "Publishing and Broadcasting Limited") form a partnership for the supply of [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network") programming to the [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") network.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-65)
*   1 April: [Southern Cross Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Broadcasting "Southern Cross Broadcasting") acquires Spencer Gulf Telecasters, gaining control of [Central GTS/BKN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTS/BKN "GTS/BKN") in parts of regional [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia "South Australia") and [Broken Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Hill,_New_South_Wales "Broken Hill, New South Wales").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-66)
*   22 June: The [SBS World News Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_World_News_Channel "SBS World News Channel") is officially launched by the [Minister for Communications, Information Technology and the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Communications,_Information_Technology_and_the_Arts_(Australia) "Minister for Communications, Information Technology and the Arts (Australia)"), Senator [Richard Alston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Alston_(politician) "Richard Alston (politician)").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-sbswnc-67)

2003
*   Unknown Date: [The Wiggles Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wiggles_Movie "The Wiggles Movie") (1997 Version) is recorded on Channel 7. This is because earlier in 1998, it launched as a tv series. The TV Series of the wiggles is currently on DVD.
*   22 May: The [Australian Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation") decides to close the [ABC Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)") and [Fly TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly_TV "Fly TV") channels.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-whoseabc-45)
*   22 December: [Tasmanian Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TDT_(TV_station) "TDT (TV station)"), a Network Ten affiliate, launches.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tdt-68)

2004
*   17 March: Trial [datacast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datacast "Datacast") service [Digital Forty Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Forty_Four "Digital Forty Four") begins in Sydney.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-d44history-69)
*   23 April: Community station [C31 Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C31_Adelaide "C31 Adelaide") launches.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-c31adelaide-70)
*   18 July: Senator [Helen Coonan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Coonan "Helen Coonan") becomes the Minister for Communications, Information Technology and the Arts.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-coonan-71)

2005
*   7 March: [ABC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_Plus "ABC TV Plus") launches with an episode of _[Landline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landline\_(TV\_series) "Landline (TV series)")_ at 6.35 am.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-abctwo-72)
*   10 March: ABC2 is officially inaugurated by Senator [Helen Coonan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Coonan "Helen Coonan"), at the Australian [Parliament House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Australia "Parliament of Australia") in [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra "Canberra").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-abctwo-72)
*   1 July: The [Australian Broadcasting Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Authority "Australian Broadcasting Authority") and [Australian Communications Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Communications_Authority "Australian Communications Authority") are replaced by the [Australian Communications and Media Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Communications_and_Media_Authority "Australian Communications and Media Authority").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-acmalast-73)
*   21 November: Community station [Television Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Sydney "Television Sydney") commences broadcasting.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-tvs-74)
*   12 December: The [Australian Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Government "Australian Government") renews [ABC Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australia) "ABC Television (Australia)")'s contract to manage the [Asia Pacific television service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Australia_(Southeast_Asian_TV_channel) "ABC Australia (Southeast Asian TV channel)") for five years, providing [A$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_dollar "Australian dollar")100 million in funding.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-abcap-75)

2006
*   1 January: [Mildura Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildura_Digital_Television "Mildura Digital Television"), a Network Ten affiliate, launches.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-mdt-76)
*   8 February: [Prime Television Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Television_Limited "Prime Television Limited") sells [Prime Television New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Television_New_Zealand "Prime Television New Zealand") to [Sky Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SKY_Network_Television "SKY Network Television") for [NZ$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_dollar "New Zealand dollar")30 million.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-prime00s-61)
*   18 July: _[Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_School\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)")_ celebrates 40 years
*   16 September: Australian Television's 50th anniversary.

2007
*   13 March: Channels are reserved for the introduction of [digital television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_television "Digital television") to remote areas such as [Alice Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Springs "Alice Springs"), [Mount Isa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Isa "Mount Isa"), and regional [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-acmareserved-77)
*   28 March: The Australian Communications and Media Authority extends [Digital Forty Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Forty_Four "Digital Forty Four")'s trial datacast licence.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-d44history-69)
*   18 May: ACMA grants a licence to [Darwin Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_Digital_Television "Darwin Digital Television"), owned by [PBL Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBL_Media "PBL Media") and Southern Cross Broadcasting.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-acma-78)
*   30 May: [Southern Cross Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Broadcasting "Southern Cross Broadcasting") announces the sale of [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") station [NWS-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWS_(TV_station) "NWS (TV station)") to [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") for $105 million.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-79)
*   8 June: WIN Television completes its takeover of [STW-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STW "STW")[Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth") for $163.1 million.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-80)
*   13 June: [C31 Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C31_Adelaide "C31 Adelaide")'s trial licence is extended for a further twelve months.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-c31extended-81)
*   13 July: [National Indigenous Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Indigenous_Television "National Indigenous Television") launches as Australia's 'third public broadcaster'.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-82)
*   14 September: [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten "Network Ten") announces [Ten HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_HD "10 HD").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-83)
*   15 September: The [Seven Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Media_Group "Seven Media Group") announces a [high definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_television "High-definition television") multichannel, to be launched in December 2007.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-hdtv-84)
*   23 September: The Australian Government proposes a new children's multichannel, [ABC3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC3 "ABC3").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-abc3-85)
*   15 October: The [Seven Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Media_Group "Seven Media Group") launch [7HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7HD "7HD"), a [high definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_television "High-definition television") multichannel.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-86)
*   16 December: [Network Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten "Network Ten") launches [Ten HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_HD "10 HD"), a [high definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_television "High-definition television") multichannel.
*   18 December: Minister for Communications, [Stephen Conroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Conroy "Stephen Conroy") announces switch-off of analogue television signals will take place between 2010 and 2013.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-87)

2008
*   1 January: ABC TV becomes [ABC1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC TV (Australian TV channel)") and changes its logo along with [ABC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_Plus "ABC TV Plus").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-88)
*   17 March: The Nine Network launches its new [high definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_television "High-definition television") multichannel, [9HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9HD "9HD").
*   28 April: [Darwin Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_Digital_Television "Darwin Digital Television"), a Network Ten affiliate, is launched.
*   7 May: SBS TV changes its logo and its on-air look and along with it comes a new slogan - "Six Billion Stories and Counting" and SBS HD become [720p](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/720p "720p").
*   3 August: Nine airs the last ever edition of long-running Canberra-based political program, _Sunday_ after 27 years.
*   8 – 24 August: SBS TV partners up with the Seven Network for joint coverage of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games.
*   20 October: Nine relaunches _[National Nine News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine\_News "Nine News")_ as _Nine News_.
*   24 November: Freeview Australia is launched across Australia at 6:29pm

2009
*   26 March: [One HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Bold "10 Bold") launches – the first commercial digital-only network in Australia.
*   3 May: Nine launches _The Morning News Hour_ and _The Late News_ (renamed _Nightline_)
*   1 June: SBS TV becomes [SBS ONE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") and [SBS TWO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Viceland "SBS Viceland") launches on digital television.
*   9 August: [GO!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Go! "9Go!") launches on Channel 99 in Nine-owned areas and Channel 88 in WIN/NBN areas.
*   1 November: [7TWO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7two "7two") launches on Channel 72 in Seven-owned areas.
*   4 December: [ABC3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Me "ABC Me") launches on Channel 23. [ABC for Kids on 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)"), a block on [ABC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_Plus "ABC TV Plus") from 9am (on weekends, 6am) to 6pm, launches.

## 2010s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2010s")]

2010
*   1 March: [Television Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Sydney "Television Sydney") commences digital broadcasting on Channel 44.
*   10 April: Digital-only community station [West TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_TV "West TV") launches in Perth, replacing [Access 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_31 "Access 31").
*   28 May: [C31 Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C31_Melbourne "C31 Melbourne") commences digital broadcasting on Channel 44.
*   7 June: [31 Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitchhike_TV "Hitchhike TV") commences digital broadcasting on Channel 44.
*   10 June: [West Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Digital_Television "West Digital Television"), a Network Ten affiliate, commences digital broadcasting in Western Australia.
*   30 June: History is made, as Mildura/Sunraysia became the first region to shut down analogue tv.
*   22 July: [ABC News 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC News (Australian TV channel)") launches on channel 24 by the ABC as Australia's first free-to-air English news channel. (SBS originally had an international news channel)
*   25 September: [7mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7mate "7mate") launches on Channel 73 by the Seven Network, replacing [7HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7HD "7HD") on Channel 73 in Seven-owned areas and 63 in Prime areas. 7TWO changed its theme to a Best of [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom")-oriented format.
*   26 September: [GEM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Gem "9Gem") launches on Channel 90 in Nine-owned areas and Channel 80 in WIN/NBN areas replacing [9HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9HD "9HD"), two days late due to technical issues.
*   5 November: [C31 Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_44_(Adelaide) "Channel 44 (Adelaide)") launches digital broadcasting on Channel 44 as 44 Adelaide, as allocated to all metropolitan community television services.
*   1 December: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") commences broadcast of Network Ten in the [Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrumbidgee_Irrigation_Area "Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area").
*   10 December: [Viewer Access Satellite Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viewer_Access_Satellite_Television "Viewer Access Satellite Television") launches for NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, TAS and NT, for viewers who cannot get TV Reception from their transmitters.

2011
*   11 January: [Eleven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Peach "10 Peach") launches on Channel 11 in Metro and Channel 55 in Regional areas.
*   16 January: The Big Red "7" logo expands to Prime & GWN as names [Prime7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime7 "Prime7") and [GWN7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GWN7 "GWN7")
*   2 May: [Central Digital Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Digital_Television "Central Digital Television"), a Network Ten affiliate, commences digital broadcasting in remote areas. [ABC for Kids on 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)") rebrands as _ABC4 Kids_, and expands its time to 6am to 7pm.
*   8 May: One HD rebrands as _[One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10\_Bold "10 Bold")_, launching the format with entertainment targeting 25 to 54-year-old men.
*   18 July: _[Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_School\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)")_ celebrates its 45-year anniversary.
*   28 July: The channels: 7TWO, GO!, GEM, One, Eleven & 7mate, became available in Albany/Bunbury.
*   16 September: Television in Australia celebrates its 55th anniversary.
*   18 September: [Television 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4ME "4ME") launches on Channel 64 in Prime areas.
*   December: Television 4 rebrands as _[TV4ME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4ME "4ME")_ and launches on Channel 74 in Seven-owned areas.
*   11 November – February 2012: 7TWO, GO!, GEM, One, Eleven & 7mate launches in Mount Gambier/Riverland.

2012
*   13 January: WIN Television commenced broadcasting of GEM, GO!, One, and Eleven in the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area (MIA).
*   4 March: NBN Television (The first regional television station in NSW as NBN-3 Newcastle) celebrates broadcasting for 50 years to Newcastle and Northern NSW, from as far south as the [Central Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Coast,_New_South_Wales "Central Coast, New South Wales") to as far north as the Gold Coast and as far west as [Gunnedah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnedah "Gunnedah").
*   26 March: [Extra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_(Australian_TV_channel) "Extra (Australian TV channel)") launches on Channel 94 in Eastern Seaboard Metro Markets and Channel 84 in the Northern NSW market.
*   20 April: WIN Television commenced broadcasting of 7mate in the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area (MIA) on LCN 60.
*   1 May: [WIN Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_(Australian_TV_channel) "Gold (Australian TV channel)") launches on Channel 84 and Channel 94 in metropolitan areas Perth and Adelaide.
*   5 May: WIN Gold rebrands as _[Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold\_(Australian\_TV\_channel) "Gold (Australian TV channel)")_.
*   5 June: WIN Television commenced broadcasting of 7TWO in the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area (MIA) on LCN 66.
*   24 September: Network Ten to commence broadcasting of datacasting channel [TVSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVSN "TVSN") on LCN 14.
*   27 November: Shutdown of analogue television services: Northern NSW
*   12 December: [NITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Indigenous_Television "National Indigenous Television") commences free-to-air broadcast via SBS

2013
*   Conversion from analogue to digital television is completed: Shutdown of analogue television services: Adelaide SA (2 April); Tasmania (9 April); Perth WA (16 April); Brisbane, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast QLD (28 May); Regional and Remote WA (25 June); Darwin NT (30 July); Sydney, Central Coast NSW (3 December); Melbourne VIC, Remote Central and Eastern Australia (10 December).
*   1 April: SBS relaunches digital channel SBS TWO (SBS 2) with a focus on the under-40 age group.
*   C31 Melbourne, C31 Adelaide, C31 Perth, C31 Brisbane, and TVS C31 Sydney goes to Digital 44.
*   13 July: Gold’s 5 hour timeshift channel, [Gold 2 (Australian TV Channel)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_2_(Australian_TV_Channel)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Gold 2 (Australian TV Channel) (page does not exist)") is launched on LCN 82 in WIN, VTV, Queensland and Tasmania WIN Channels.

2014
*   2 February: [GO!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Go! "9Go!") changes its branding and logo to new ones.
*   7 July: [ABC4 Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)") expands its time to 5am to 7pm on ABC2.
*   20 July: [ABC1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC TV (Australian TV channel)") rebrands as _ABC_.

2015
*   2 March: [ABC4 Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)") rebrands as _ABC Kids_.
*   18 March: _[Neighbours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbours "Neighbours")_ celebrates 30 years.
*   5 July: [SBS ONE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") rebrands as _SBS_.
*   29 August: [Racing.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing.com "Racing.com") (A horse racing channel) launches on channel 78 in metro places and channel 68 in regional places.
*   17 November: [Food Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Network_(Australia) "Food Network (Australia)") (SBS's fourth channel featuring food shows) launches on Channel 33, replacing [SBS 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_3 "SBS 3").
*   26 November: [9Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Life "9Life") launches on channel 94, along with a relaunch of [9HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9HD "9HD") on channel 90. [GEM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Gem "9Gem") is renamed 9Gem and moved to channel 92 and [GO!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Go! "9Go!") is renamed 9Go! and moved to channel 93 with the quality of 9Gem changed from HD to SD.
*   30 November: The [Australian Communications & Media Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Communications_&_Media_Authority "Australian Communications & Media Authority") introduced sweeping changes to the [ratings system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Commercial_Television_Code_of_Practice "Australian Commercial Television Code of Practice") for commercial networks. Among them were allowing M and MA15+ programs to air an hour earlier then they were previously allowed, from 7:30 pm and 8:30 pm respectively, PG programmes can air all day, dissolving the AV15+ classification, as well as changes to when adverts with higher classifications program can air.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-Dec15changes-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-90)

2016
*   19 January: Gold 2 shuts down and gets replaced by Extra in WIN Areas.
*   28 February: [7flix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7flix "7flix") launches on channel 76.
*   1 March: NBN relaunches [9HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9HD "9HD"), as well as [9Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Life "9Life") launching for NBN audiences.
*   1 March: WIN relaunches their version of [9HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9HD "9HD"), [WIN HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_HD "WIN HD"). [9Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Life "9Life") launches for WIN audiences.
*   2 March: Ten relaunches [Ten HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_HD "Ten HD") and the quality of [One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_(Australian_TV_channel) "One (Australian TV channel)") changes from HD to SD. WIN also relaunches [WIN HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_HD "WIN HD") and launches [9Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Life "9Life") in some areas after technical issues on the previous day.
*   30 April: [4ME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4ME "4ME") shuts down, being replaced by a simulcast of [ishop tv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishop_tv "Ishop tv") (simulcast later removed in June).
*   10 May: Seven relaunches [7HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7HD "7HD") (HD simulcast of Seven in Melbourne and Adelaide, HD simulcast of 7mate in other markets) and the quality of [7mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7mate "7mate") changes from HD to SD.
*   1 July: [Southern Cross Austereo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Austereo "Southern Cross Austereo") switches affiliation from Network Ten to the Nine Network in Southern NSW, Australian Capital Territory, Regional Queensland, Regional Victoria and Tasmania.
*   1 July: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") switches affiliation from the Nine Network to Network Ten in Southern NSW, Australian Capital Territory, Regional Queensland, Regional Victoria, Mildura, Regional WA, Tasmania and Eastern SA.
*   1 July: Extra on WIN Regions: Southern NSW, ACT, Regional Queensland, Regional Victoria, Mildura, Regional WA, Tasmania and Eastern SA and gets replaced by a placeholder with some music in the background, which is similar to [Viewer Access Satellite Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viewer_Access_Satellite_Television "Viewer Access Satellite Television") scenic loop on Regional News Channels. The Channels Range as WIN on Channel 8, WIN HD on Channel 80, ONE on Channel 81, Eleven on Channel 82, TVSN on Channel 84 and GOLD on Channel 85.
*   17 July: [9Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Life "9Life") relaunches in Southern NSW, Australian Capital Territory, Regional Queensland and Regional Victoria due to the affiliate swap.
*   18 July: [Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_School_(Australian_TV_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)") celebrates 50 years.
*   16 September: 60th anniversary of television in Australia.
*   19 September: [ABC3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Me "ABC Me") rebrands as _ABC Me_.
*   15 November: [SBS 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Viceland "SBS Viceland")_rebrands_ as SBS Viceland.
*   6 December: ABC relaunches [ABC HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_HD_(Australia) "ABC HD (Australia)") and the quality of [ABC News 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC News (Australian TV channel)") changes from HD to SD.

2017
*   1 January: [ABC Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)") expands its time to 5am to 7.30pm, ABC2 also expands its time to 7:30pm to 2am.
*   23 March: [Southern Cross Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Television "Southern Cross Television") relaunches a high definition simulcast of their main channel, _Southern Cross HD_, in Tasmania on channel 60.
*   8 April: SBS launches a high definition simulcast of [SBS Viceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Viceland "SBS Viceland") on channel 31.
*   10 April: ABC News 24 rebrands as _ABC News_.
*   17 April: [Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage_(TV_program) "Rage (TV program)") celebrates 30 years.
*   31 May: WIN Television purchases [NRN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRN "NRN") from Southern Cross.
*   1 July: On the WIN Network, music got replaced by a voiceover.
*   4 December: [ABC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_Plus "ABC TV Plus")_rebrands_ as ABC Comedy.

2018
*   2 September: [Sky News on WIN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_News_Australia "Sky News Australia") (now Sky News Regional) was launched on free-to-air TV in regional Australia.
*   1 October: [Your Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your_Money_(TV_channel) "Your Money (TV channel)") launches to be broadcast on channel 95/85.
*   31 October: Network 10 launches a major network branding. Channel Ten becomes [Channel 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_10 "Network 10"), while multichannels ONE and ELEVEN are rebranded as 10 Boss (later renamed to [10 Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Bold "10 Bold")) and [10 Peach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Peach "10 Peach") respectively.
*   17 November: Food Network rebrands to [SBS Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Food "SBS Food").
*   1 December: [7food network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7food_network "7food network") launches on channel 74.

2019
*   8 February: The [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network"), the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network"), [Network 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_10 "Network 10") and [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") along with regional networks [Prime7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime7 "Prime7"), [GWN7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GWN7 "GWN7"), [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television"), [NBN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBN_(TV_station) "NBN (TV station)") stopped using full-screen and voiced-over [classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Commercial_Television_Code_of_Practice "Australian Commercial Television Code of Practice") warning boards before the beginning of a program. However, [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC (Australian TV channel)") continues to use full-screen and voiced-over boards before the start of a program.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-91), now showing classifications at the very start of the show/movie instead.
*   17 May: [Your Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your_Money_(TV_channel) "Your Money (TV channel)") ceases to broadcast on channel 95/85.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-92)
*   June: 9Gem HD launches on the space vacated by Your Money; in Darwin on 14 June; in Adelaide, Brisbane and Perth on 20 June; and in Sydney and Melbourne on 21 June.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-93)
*   20 June: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") axes four local news bulletins, which were, the Central West, Riverina, Border North East ([Albury-Wodonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albury-Wodonga "Albury-Wodonga")) and the [Wide Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Bay-Burnett "Wide Bay-Burnett") because of insufficient commercial viability to fund those regional news operations.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-94)

## 2020s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Timeline_of_Australian_television&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2020s")]

2020
*   16 January: Seven launches a high definition simulcast of [7mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7mate "7mate") on channel 74.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-95)
*   5 April: [9Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9Rush "9Rush") launches on channel 96.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-96)
*   27 September: [10 Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Shake "10 Shake") launches on channel 13.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-97)

2021
*   1 January: ABC Comedy _rebrands_ as [ABC TV Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_TV_Plus "ABC TV Plus"), returning to its general entertainment format.
*   1 July: [Southern Cross Austereo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Austereo "Southern Cross Austereo") switches affiliation back to Network Ten from the Nine Network in most markets.
*   1 July: [WIN Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIN_Television "WIN Television") switches affiliation back to the Nine Network from Network Ten in most markets. (excluding [NRN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRN "NRN"))
*   18 July: [Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_School_(Australian_TV_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)") celebrates 55 years.
*   16 September: 65th anniversary of television in Australia.

2022
*   28 July: The final episode of _[Neighbours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbours "Neighbours")_ goes to air on [Network 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_10 "Network 10") and [10 Peach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Comedy "10 Comedy").

2023
*   15 January: [7Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7Bravo "7Bravo") launches on channel 75.
*   12 April: [Southern Cross Austereo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_Austereo "Southern Cross Austereo")-owned [GTS/BKN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTS/BKN "GTS/BKN") cancels its long-running regional news service effectively immediately. ending over 50 years of news operations for the [Spencer Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Gulf "Spencer Gulf") and [Broken Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Hill "Broken Hill") regions
*   1 August: [10 Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Shake "10 Shake") rebrands as [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon_(Australian_TV_channel) "Nickelodeon (Australian TV channel)").
*   16 August: 11.15 million people nationwide view the semi-final of the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup "2023 FIFA Women's World Cup") between Australia's [Matildas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matildas "Matildas") and England's [Lionesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_women's_national_football_team "England women's national football team").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Australian_television#cite_note-98)

2024
*   3 June: ABC TV Plus rebrands to [ABC Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Family_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC Family (Australian TV channel)"), ABC Me rebrands to [ABC Entertains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Entertains "ABC Entertains").
*   12 June: 10 Bold rebranded to [10 Bold Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Bold_Drama "10 Bold Drama"), 10 Peach rebranded to [10 Peach Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Peach_Comedy "10 Peach Comedy").
*   6 October: [C31 Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C31_Melbourne "C31 Melbourne") celebrates 30 years of community TV broadcasting.

2025
*   18 March: _[Neighbours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbours "Neighbours")_ celebrates 40 years.
*   1 July: 10 Peach Comedy and 10 Bold Drama were both replaced by ‘10 Comedy’ and ‘10 Drama’ to embrace their real genres of their channels.
*   11 August: Southern Cross Austereo owned Tasmania cancels its long-running regional news service effectively immediately, ending over 50 years of news operations for the Tasmania region.
*   22 October: Foxtel celebrates 30 years.

2026
*   7 January: Seven West Media merges with Southern Cross Media.
*   18 July: [Play School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_School_(Australian_TV_series) "Play School (Australian TV series)") celebrates 60 years.
*   16 September: 70th anniversary of television in Australia.

2027
*   17 April: [Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage_(TV_program) "Rage (TV program)") celebrates 40 years.
